prerequisites: It is recommended to have completed the 1st year Chemistry course of the Engineering Degree.

learning_outcomes.text: Know the principles and basic operations of Chemical Analysis.
Know the fundamentals, instrumentation, and applications of instrumental analysis techniques with greater relevance in the industrial field.
Know the properties and basic reactivity of organic compounds.
Differentiate the behavior of organic and inorganic compounds.
Formulate and solve problems in the field of the Advanced Chemistry course.
Apply the techniques used in a basic Analytical Chemistry and Organic Chemistry laboratory, including the necessary calculations and expressing the results appropriately.
Prepare and present correctly a report, both orally and in writing, corresponding to one of the practices carried out in the Advanced Chemistry course.

syllabus_topics: Topic 1. Basic operations of chemical analysis.
Topic 2. Classical methods of analysis. Gravimetric methods. Volumetric methods.

Topic 3. Instrumental methods of analysis. Introduction to instrumental analysis. Introduction to spectroscopic techniques. Introduction to techniques based on mass spectrometry. Introduction to chromatographic techniques. Introduction to electrochemical methods.
Topic 4. Saturated hydrocarbons. Classification of hydrocarbons. Ways to represent an organic molecule. Conformational analysis in acyclic and cyclic systems: alkanes and cycloalkanes.

Topic 5. Stereochemistry. Isomerism. Types of isomerism. Chirality. Optical activity. Absolute configuration: R/S nomenclature. Fischer projection. Molecules with more than one chiral center: diastereomers and meso forms. Enantiomers. Racemic mixture.
Topic 6. Unsaturated hydrocarbons. Alkenes and alkynes: addition reactions. Benzene stability: aromaticity.

Topic 7. Compounds with C–X, C–O and C–N single bonds. Alkyl halides: nucleophilic substitution reactions and elimination reactions. Alcohols, and phenols, ethers and amines: structure, nomenclature, physical and chemical properties.
Topic 8. Aldehydes, ketones, carbohydrates. Structure and nomenclature. Addition reactions to the carbonyl group: water, alcohols and amines. Keto-enol tautomerism. Oxidation-reduction reactions.
Topic 9. Carboxylic acids and acid derivatives. Structure and nomenclature. Acidity of carboxylic acids. Salt formation: soaps. Esterification. Hydrolysis of esters and saponification. Amides.
Determination of chemical elements by atomic absorption and/or emission spectroscopy.
Separation of a mixture of compounds by gas chromatography.
Basic operations in an Organic Chemistry laboratory: extraction, distillation, and recrystallization.

assessment_methods.method: Written tests and/or evaluable activities (Block I - March, Block II - May)
Classroom Practices, Group Tutorials, and Laboratory Practices (Teaching Folder)

assessment_rules: In the ordinary call, a minimum grade of 4 out of 10 must be obtained in each written test (Block I and Block II) to aspire to the overall grade. A minimum grade of 4 out of 10 is also required in the respective teaching folders. The final grade must be 5 or higher out of 10. For extraordinary calls, a final written exam will be held covering all topics and laboratory practices, with a minimum passing grade of 5 out of 10. Students who passed one block with a 5 or higher can choose to only be evaluated on the failed block in the extraordinary call, and the final grade will be the average of both blocks.
